data.body: Phase 1 classification (2026-08-17): the reported mechanism is CONFIRMED, but the not-a-bug guard classifies the requested behavior as `feature-request` / current `intended-behavior`, so Phase 2 is locked pending an explicit contract change. Runtime reproduction with `[reconciler] rich_text_cutover = "clould"` showed `rebar config validate` exit 0 with `OK — no removed inputs are set`, while `rebar config` rejected the value as outside `[both, cloud, dc, off]`. Source tracing confirms `_validate` at `src/rebar/_commands/show_config.py:112-142` intentionally calls only `scan_tombstones`; it does not call typed resolution. Authoritative contract: `docs/config.md:577-585` explicitly defines this command as a non-raising sweep of every tombstoned input, non-zero iff an error-class tombstone is present; the command docstring/help and `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_tombstone_registry.py:217-228` encode the same behavior. Git blame/history shows implementation, docs, and tests were introduced together in commit 3eb3e71337, ruling out an accidental regression. Recommended non-fix disposition absent a product decision: close/reclassify as not-a-bug. If the user explicitly approves broadening the command contract, treat that as a feature-scope decision and define the aggregation semantics before RED/GREEN implementation.
